evidence.text: The Government’s ON Program will develop a national infrastructure to offer open access, wholesale broadband telecommunications services.

extra_evidence.text: This subcomponent will support construction and activation of high‐ capacity middle‐mile, backhaul networks under the ON Program that will bring high quality, high‐capacity services to selected rural settlements.
SPs will then invest to expand their networks to provide services on commercial terms through their own last‐mile infrastructures, to the settlements’ households, enterprises, and organizations.
The Project will support Georgia’s Open Net Program to develop national infrastructure to offer open access, wholesale, broadband‐telecommunications services.
It will finance: (i) Design and construction of an open access, wholesale broadband telecommunications network to connect selected rural settlements;

(ii) Acquisition of connectivity services to operate the network; and (iii) Consultancies as needed to support network design, readiness and demand assessments, deployment, operations, maintenance, and upgrades.
Subcomponent 1.1 supports the creation of middle‐mile networks as part of the Open Net Program of the Government.
In 2015, the Government set up a National Program on Broadband Infrastructure Development (henceforth, the ‘Open Net Program’) to improve middle‐mile connectivity in rural areas.
The Government has defined this program as seeking to replicate, as closely as feasible, the RAIN Program of Lithuania, which has received significant funding from the European Union.
The Project will finance the construction of middle‐mile networks to connect selected settlements and to establish open access points of presence (PoPs) at those settlements.

The Project will finance the design, building, installation, and activation of backhaul infrastructure for up to about 1,000 settlements identified by the ComCom as eligible (of a total of 3,388 settlements across Georgia); most of the rest of the settlements will be covered by a pilot program financed by the GoG using its own resources, and some settlements might not be eligible in the future.

The network will include sections that are newly constructed and, where suitable existing infrastructure exists, the program will use that infrastructure either through leasing of capacity or the purchase of indefeasible rights of use (IRUs).

category.rationale: Operational: re-engineers broadband delivery via wholesale open access

sector.rationale: Finances construction of middle-mile backhaul network infrastructure.
